newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares retreat as coalition optimism melts.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares retreat as coalition optimism melts.

text.p: Turkish shares retreated from record highs on Tuesday as hopes of a secularist coalition began to melt away in the face of right-wing division, brokers said.
The True Path Party's rejection of a rival conservative's offer to join an anti-Islamist alliance eroded nearly half of the massive eight percent gains posted on Monday.
The IMKB National-100 index sank 3.49 percent, or 62 points, to end the morning session at 1,712. Trading volume slipped to 20.76 trillion lira ($142 million) from 21.59 trillion on Monday.
"The market was irritated by the possibility that the conservative True Path Party may not support the new alliance," said Okan Gulek from Taksim Securities.

True Path leader Tansu Ciller, allied with the Islamists of outgoing prime minister Necmettin Erbakan, was to meet her rival Mesut Yilmaz on Tuesday despite her party's decision to rebuff his alliance offer. The decision unleashed profit-taking.
"I view the sales that we are seeing as profit-taking after the rapid gains yesterday," said broker Huseyin Aladag of Turk Ticaret Securities.
Utility Cukurova Elektrik and flat steel maker Eregli led share activity, brokers said.
The heavy wave of selling was exacerbated by the comments of leftist leader Deniz Baykal, who agreed to support a Yilmaz-led coalition but told supporters he sought elections by the end of the year.
"Baykal's remarks also had a negative effect. Sales may continue," Gulek said.
Yilmaz has said he did not want to take the country to polls before next spring. He was asked last week to replace Erbakan who stepped down after months of army criticism.
Yilmaz is short of the simple majority needed in parliament to win a confidence vote even with the support of two left-wing parties and a right-wing group which broke away from the DYP.

A core of optimism about the prospects for a secularist coalition underpinned the market. But shares were expected to remain vulnerable to any negative signals emerging from talks between political leaders, brokers said.

"Our expectations for political developments are reasonably positive. But if an agreement cannot be reached then uncertainty could once more take control of the market," said Toprak Securities broker Vedat Konyyali.
The Turkish lira eased to 146,460 to the dollar, compared with the central bank's key dollar rate of 146,200 on Monday.
Bond yields edged higher after sharp declines to around 100 percent on Monday from 105 percent. The most active bond's yield rose slightly to 100.78 pct from 100.55 pct.
